text: The three days of travel in Genesis 22 are to be read as a suspended sentence. Outwardly nothing happens; in truth all that matters is happening. The servants are mentioned, and the wood, the knife, and the fire; the implements of the act are named before the act itself has occurred. Obedience and horror remain side by side in the narrative, and neither prevails over the other. Feeling is no measure of the faith shown here; its form is an arrangement of fixed relations, like a geometry, in Genesis 22.
